_comment: How the game turns the map data in data/city/ into a town. Coordinates are never typed here: places are named by the streets that meet there, and the game looks them up in the OSM data.

map.name: Sand Bar
map._comment: Which map this is. Trans-Canada Auto is meant to grow a map at a time (one config like this per map); Sand Bar is the first.

origin._comment: World (0,0,0). This is the OSM position of the Great George Street / Richmond Street junction (node 8598664). Keep it fixed when the map grows so existing coordinates stay valid.

play_area._comment: The playable area: the bypass ring (Riverside Drive, the Arterial Highway, Upton Road), closed by the North River and the harbour. 'ring' goes round the edge in order: 'streets' is a junction named by two streets that meet there, and between two such junctions the edge follows the shortest way along the streets in 'follow' ("" lets it through the unnamed roundabouts on Riverside Drive). 'water' is a point out in the river or harbour as [latitude, longitude], the one place coordinates are typed, since water has no street names. The invisible wall sits margin_m outside this line, with road-closed barriers wherever a street crosses it.

ring._comment: the North River, where the Trans-Canada crosses to Cornwall
the Hillsborough River, past the bridge

spawn._comment: The player starts in the aisle of a parkade (its OSM id, a landmark with style parkade): on 'level' (0 is the ground floor), in front of 'stall' (counting from the far end, away from the entrance) on 'side' (1 or -1 of the ramp). Without 'parkade': on the sidewalk at the junction of 'streets', facing the 'face_toward' junction.

parked_cars._comment: Cars parked at the start. In a parkade: backed into 'stall' on 'level' and 'side' (as for the spawn). Otherwise against the right-hand curb: on 'street', 'distance_m' from the junction with 'from', heading toward 'toward'. 'model' is an id in scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd; 'colour' is a hex colour or the model's first colour if left out.

work_yard._comment: The truck yard: the McQuaid's Moving and Storage lot off Riverside Drive (OSM way 297177033). Its lidar trees stand in islands; everything here sits in the drive aisles between them, clear of the trunks. 'pos' (longitude, latitude) is the middle of the lot and 'direction' the compass heading its long side runs, the same as a map editor spot. Each vehicle and load is placed by 'at': metres [right, back] from the middle, facing 'direction' turned by 'heading' degrees clockwise; 'lift' raises a load (1.52 puts it on a flatbed trailer's deck). Vehicle 'model' ids are in scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd and truck_models.gd; load 'kind's are in scripts/vehicles/cargo.gd.

fleet_cars._comment: Fleet cars, always where they are here even when the map editor places the other cars: model (scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd), livery (CarModels.LIVERIES), unit (the number on the plate and sides), pos [longitude, latitude] and direction (compass degrees the nose points). The Charlatown Police Services squad cars, nosed in along the station's south-east wall on Kirkwood Drive (Joe's note: Dodge Journeys and some Dodge Rams; ours are Dodgy Jaunts and Rammers).

road_defaults._comment: By OSM highway class: curb-to-curb width (two-way and one-way), sidewalk width, and for highways the paved shoulder outside the edge line. When OSM gives a lane count the width is lanes x lane + both shoulders. A class with a shoulder is built highway style: no curbs or sidewalks, white edge lines, gravel verges.

minor_roads._comment: Roads outside drivable_classes that are still built, plain asphalt with no curbs, sidewalks or paint (see road_defaults): OSM service roads whose service= value is listed here ('' is a service road with none: the lanes through a campus, a hospital, a lot or an industrial park, like Lily Pond Drive and the Ravenwood Drives), and tracks with a name (Wharf Road, Ferry Road). Driveways, parking aisles and drive-throughs stay painted on the ground. Pieces underground (layer below 0) are left out.

street_overrides._comment: Widths measured against OSM building footprints (median gap between building fronts across each street, inside the play area). Curb + sidewalk must stay inside that gap.

brick_streets._comment: Victoria Row: the brick block of Richmond Street between Queen and Great George.

landmarks._comment: Extra detail for well-known buildings, matched by OSM way id. Footprints still come from OSM; these set what the footprint can't tell us. Colours, heights and towers are best estimates, not measurements. Entries can be small: one that only sets colours or materials keeps the building's measured lidar height and roof (set wall_height or roof to override those). Keys: style (brick, clapboard, sandstone, painted, modern, shingle, church), colour, roof_colour, spire_colour, wall_height (m), roof (flat, gabled or hipped), pitch (degrees), chimneys (how many, in pairs along the ridge of a pitched roof), trim (white, cream, green, black), shop, awning (a colour, or none), sign (a name board over the front), cornice (false for a plain top), towers (front_pair, front_center, front_corner), tower_size, tower_height, spire_height, tower_protrude (m), portico, portico_width, ribbed (ribbed sandstone with slot windows), massing ("confederation" for its extra blocks), and where the front is: front_toward [street, street] (faces that junction), front_toward_spot [latitude, longitude] (faces that spot, e.g. where a field note was taken) or front_street; front_line: main runs the front along the main wall the whole width of the building, past vestibules standing out of it. Big stores and plazas: roof mansard (a sloping skirt of shingles round a flat top) with eave_height, roof_top and roof_overhang (m out from the walls, a covered walk on posts when over 1 m), shopfront: front (shop glass on the front wall only), style: tank (a white storage tank with a stair up its side; roof cone or dome, dome_width, sign and logo for an oil company's name between chevrons), and entrances, a list of tall glass A-frames through the roof, each {at (0 to 1 along the front from its left end as you face it), width, depth, ridge, sign, sign_colour, sign_text}; one without a sign shows the brand's name. An entrance with shape: tower is a flat-topped glass tower instead (Princess Auto's): height, cap, cap_colour, doors (height of the shop doors), band {colour, text, text_colour, reach} a canopy over the doors with text on its edge, accent {colour, width, side} a strip of colour on the wall beside it. wall_signs: a list of names or logos on walls other than the front, each {facing (compass degrees the wall looks toward), at (0 to 1 along it from its left end as you face it), sign, sign_colour ("wall" for letters straight on the wall), sign_text, sign_height, sign_y}. base_colour and base_height put a base course along the front of a store with entrances; windows: false leaves the walls blank. Quick oil changes built the Pro Oil way: barrel {height, radius} (a round tower like an oil drum, the way in, with the name on it; it stands on the footprint's round part, or the front's right-hand corner) and bay_doors (drive-through bays, a door at each end down both long sides). Strip plazas: units, the shops along the front left to right, each {from, to (0 to 1 along the front from its left end as you face it), colour (its facade over the shop glass), height (a raised parapet over the roof, m), glass (false for a blank wall), band (a dark canopy fascia over the glass), sign, sign_colour (the board, else the facade's colour), sign_text, sign_height}; each stands on the footprint's own front wall where it is; front_depth (m, default 6) is how far back from the front line walls still get shop glass. Any building: base_colour and base_height (a brick base course round the walls), cap_colour and cap_height (a band of colour along the top edge). Quick oil changes built the Pro Oil way: barrel {height, radius} (a round tower like an oil drum, the way in, with the name on it; it stands on the footprint's round part, or the front's right-hand corner) and bay_doors (drive-through bays, a door at each end down both long sides).

28326012.name: Queen Parkade, 222 Queen Street
28326012._comment: A parkade you can drive up through (scripts/world/parkade.gd): style parkade, levels (decks, ground floor and open roof included), entrance_street (the end facing it is the way in at grade), roof_jump (a timber and plywood stunt ramp in a corner of the roof at the entrance end, angled to throw you off the corner and down the street: true, or {corner: 1 or -1, angle: degrees off the length of the roof, default 60}), at (a spot on it, for the spawn and the cars parked in it). Ground floor, two covered decks and the roof; the lidar's 12.2 m top is the stair tower.

28326014.name: Pownal Parkade, 100 Pownal Street
28326014._comment: Set into the slope: the way in is at the low end, where OSM's two driveways meet it; the far end's ground is nearly a storey higher.

28331937.name: Fitzroy Parkade, 130 Fitzroy Street
28331937._comment: OSM gives it 5 levels; the lidar's 14.9 m top fits a roof deck at 12 m and the stair tower.

390620572.name: Take 5 Oil Change (built as a Pro Oil Change), University Avenue
390620572._comment: From Joe's note: built for Pro Oil Change (Valvoline's Atlantic brand, bought out by Take 5), a build-out Pro Oil used in other towns too. A low flat-roofed box with drive-through bays (doors down both long sides) and a round tower like a 20 ft oil drum standing out of one end. OSM maps the drum's curve in the footprint, and the 2020 lidar shows the roof at 4.6 m with one spot at 6.1 m right over it.

713706292.name: Ford dealer, St Peters Road
713706292._comment: From Joe's field note: built as a plain Fjord dealer (our Ford, the Halfton's make), no local business name, with a glass showroom facing St Peters Road and trucks for sale out front. OSM names the dealership, not the make, so the brand is set here. The lidar calls the roof gabled (parts of it stand higher), but it's a flat-roofed building, so the roof is set flat.

605896236.name: Chevrolet dealer, St Peters Road
605896236._comment: From Joe's field note: built as a plain Chevalet dealer (our Chevrolet), no local business name, with a glass showroom facing St Peters Road and cars for sale on the ground between it and the road (the lot isn't mapped). OSM gives it the brand General Motors, so the make is set here. The real one (Hillside) sells Chevrolet, Buick and GMC under one roof, so Chevalet's stock includes General Motives' cars too.

259215797.name: Toyota dealer, Riverside Drive
259215797._comment: Charlottetown Toyota. OSM names the business but gives no brand, so the make (Toyola, our Toyota) is set here.

400662409.name: Honda dealer, North River Road
400662409._comment: Capital Honda. OSM names the business but gives no brand, so the make (Hanaka, our Honda) is set here.

695948071.name: Reliable Motors, John Yeo Drive
695948071._comment: From Joe's note: Reliable Motors is the Dodge dealer, just outside the map's ring. OSM names the business but gives no brand, so the make (Dodgy, our Dodge and Chrysler) is set here.

28325869.name: Province House
28325869._comment: From Joe's photos coming down Great George Street (2026-11-23): weathered grey-buff sandstone, a low hipped slate roof with chimneys, and the columned portico facing Grafton Street and the war memorial.

28325849.name: Confederation Centre of the Arts
28325849._comment: Wallace sandstone, ribbed, with slot windows. 'massing' adds the theatre fly tower, Memorial Hall and the gallery clerestory on top of the one OSM footprint, and a glazed lobby facing Queen Street.

28325878.name: Hon. George Coles Building
28325878._comment: Red brick with tall round-arched windows in Joe's photo from Great George Street (2026-11-23).

28344690.name: Birchwood Intermediate School
28344690._comment: From Joe's note 1: it's Birchwood Intermediate School (OSM has no name for it). Height and flat roof come from the lidar.

404245466.name: Charlottetown Police Services, Kirkwood Drive
404245466._comment: From Joe's note 5: the city police station, spoofed as the Charlatown Police Services (CPS, like the real one; the city's name does the joke). Navy board with white letters, facing Kirkwood Drive where the note was taken. Walls, height and flat roof still come from OSM and the lidar until there's a photo.

253239382._comment: Grafton and Prince, north-west corner: yellow clapboard with an outside stair (Joe's photo, 2026-11-23).

256712135.name: Polyclinic Professional Centre
256712135._comment: Red brick office block past Grafton and Prince (Joe's photo, 2026-11-23).

251217762.name: The Grafton Prince
251217762._comment: Newer apartments at Grafton and Prince: white siding with dark window frames and balconies (Joe's photo, 2026-11-23).

256469833.name: Centre for Community Engagement
256469833._comment: Holland College, on Grafton at Cumberland: red brick with tall blind arches and a white cornice (Joe's photo, 2026-11-23).

693082271.name: Cumberland Residence
693082271._comment: Holland College residence across Grafton: four storeys of red brick with cream trim (Joe's photo, 2026-11-23).

256471126.name: Glendenning Hall
256471126._comment: Holland College residence: pale yellow siding over a brick ground floor (only the siding is shown), white trim (Joe's photo, 2026-11-23).

28331664.name: Atlantic Superstore, University Avenue
28331664._comment: From Joe's photo from the lot off University Avenue (at the Belvedere Avenue corner): a long low store under a deep mansard of brownish-grey shingles that comes down over a covered walk on white posts, glass all along the front under it, and two tall glass A-frame entrances standing up through the roof, the clothing store at the left (south) end and the grocery near the right. Heights are read off the photo against the cars in the lot.

entrances._comment: the clothing store (Joe Fresh), its own door at the south end
the grocery's main doors, over the vestibule OSM maps standing out of the front; the sign is the brand's name, blue as on the real one

28331677.name: Strip plaza beside the Atlantic Superstore, University Avenue
28331677._comment: From Joe's two photos from the Superstore lot (University Avenue at Belvedere): a long low strip of shops facing the lot, glass along the front, each shop with its own facade and sign, left to right from the University Avenue end: Indigo (Indago) in a raised navy box, GoodLife Fitness 24 (GoodLift) in a raised pale grey one, grey filler units, Hart (Stag) in a tall red tower between lower red bays, a pale pilaster, then a lower dark run under a canopy: a red-lettered shop (sign unreadable in the photos), CIBC (Imperial Commerce), Sherwin-Williams Paints (Sherman-Wilkins) on a blue board, a small dark red unit, and a raised tan unit at the far end with teal letters (Coastline). Widths are read off the photos; heights against the cars and trucks in the lot.

units._comment: Hart, whose sign has a stag's head
red letters on the dark front; the real name isn't readable in the photos
teal letters beginning 'Coast', the rest not readable

390615844.name: Burger King, Superstore lot at University and Belvedere
390615844._comment: From Joe's photos from the Superstore lot and through the drive-thru: a low flat-roofed box in beige stucco over a base course of brown brick, a thin red stripe along the top of the parapet, and a taller brown entrance tower at the south-east corner with the round logo (Burger Baron's name here). The drive-thru runs down the west side (clearance bar, menu boards and order post on the building side of the lane, placed in edits.json) and back along the south wall to the window.

units._comment: the brown entrance tower with the round logo

158560854.name: Irving oil terminal, domed tank
158560854._comment: From Joe's photo from the Tim Hortons drive-thru at Grafton Street and Riverside Drive: white steel tanks across Riverside Drive, stairs spiralling up their sides, and this one with a white dome and the oil company's name between a red chevron and a blue one. The name is the world brand's (Ervin's for Irving). OSM has the round footprints as plain buildings; the lidar gives the heights and the dome.

222354381.name: Irving station, Riverside Drive
222354381._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. OSM maps the canopy over the pumps as the building; the store is behind it.

28433999.name: Blue warehouse, Riverside Drive
28433999._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. Long and low in blue metal siding.

28433998.name: Big grey building by the Exhibition Drive roundabout
28433998._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. Light grey siding, low pitched roof.

361875735.name: Vogue Optical, St Peters Road roundabout
361875735._comment: From Joe's photo coming up St Peters Road into the Belvedere roundabout: pale blue-grey metal siding under a dark slate roof, with CONTACT LENSES in white letters on the side facing St Peters Road.

627019671.name: Discounters, St Peters Road
627019671._comment: From Joe's photo coming up St Peters Road into the Belvedere roundabout. A plain low store; its tall sign out by St Peters Road is a placed sign in edits.json.

1092239557.name: Esso canopy, St Peters Road roundabout
1092239557._comment: From Joe's photo coming up St Peters Road into the Belvedere roundabout: across the roundabout the canopy over the pumps is a bright red band, the store behind it. OSM maps the canopy as building=roof.

422497523.name: Princess Auto, St Dunstan Street
422497523._comment: From Joe's photo from the lot in front: a big box in light grey insulated metal panels over a grey split-face block base, and a tall glass entrance tower standing out of the front (the 11 m bump OSM maps in the footprint) and up past the roof, the brand's blue sign on the glass, a yellow canopy over the doors with the tagline on it, and a blue panel on the wall to its right. Built as Countess Auto, our Princess Auto. Heights are read off the photo against the pickups parked out front; the lidar's top (8.1 m) agrees with the wall.

wall_signs._comment: the grey logo on the east side wall

band.text: A Unique World of Stuff You Didn't Know You Needed

entrances._comment: the glass entrance tower, about 14 m from the left (west) end of the front

255422625.name: Sobeys, Babineau Avenue
255422625._comment: From Joe's photo from beside Princess Auto, looking across the lot at the backs of Sobeys and PetSmart: Sobeys is the big tan-brown block on the right, with units on the roof. Only the colour is set; the lidar keeps its height and roof.

255422626.name: PetSmart, Babineau Avenue
255422626._comment: From the same photo: the darker brown block beside Sobeys, the blue PetSmart letters showing on it. OSM doesn't name it, so the brand is set here (PetDumb, our PetSmart).

wall_signs._comment: the blue name on the back, toward the left (east) end as seen from Princess Auto's lot

470328504.name: Canadian Tire, St Dunstan Street
470328504._comment: From Joe's photo across the lot from Princess Auto: a flat roof, not the gable the lidar guessed (the roof steps up in places). Height from the lidar top.

_red_crosswalks_comment: Marked crosswalks within this many metres of the origin are painted red and white, as downtown's are (Joe's photos at Great George and Grafton); further out they're plain white zebras.

monuments.name: Prince Edward Island War Memorial
monuments._comment: In front of Province House's portico, on the green by Grafton Street: three bronze soldiers advancing, on a granite pedestal (Joe's photo, 2026-11-23). Facing is a compass bearing, as in field notes.
Either side of the memorial: the Canadian flag on the left as you face Province House, the Island's on the right.

monuments.name: City of Charlatown welcome sign
monuments._comment: From Joe's photos from the Riverside Drive lights and coming off the Hillsborough Bridge (2026-11-24): the city's welcome wall on the grass by the path from the Event Grounds, about 18 degrees left of straight down Grafton Street and some 80 m off when stopped at the lights coming from Stratford, spruce behind it, the flags running west from it toward Grafton Street. It faces the junction, between Riverside Drive and the bridge. 'Bienvenue / Pjila'si / Welcome', the city's name, 'Birthplace of Confederation'. Drawn by tools/make_entrance_signs.py.

From Joe's photos (2026-11-24): a row of tall white poles running west from the welcome sign along the path toward Grafton Street, the city's flag nearest the sign, then the provinces in order of joining Confederation, the territories and Canada's. Flags drawn by tools/make_flags.py; the order past Nova Scotia is a best guess.
From Joe's photos (2026-11-24): a black picket fence behind the flags, between brick piers, the Event Grounds beyond.

monuments.name: Mural wall at the city entrance
monuments._comment: From Joe's photos from the Riverside Drive lights (2026-11-24): a low wall in the fence line behind the flags, by the welcome sign, a painted mural between brick piers, facing the road. Our own mural (tools/make_entrance_signs.py), not a copy of the real one.

From Joe's photos from the Riverside Drive lights at the Hillsborough Bridge (2026-11-24): on the island between Riverside Drive's southbound lanes and the right-turn lane to Grafton Street, before the lights: the black lane-use sign (two lefts for the bridge, a lane that ends, a right for Grafton) over a yellow hazard marker.

monuments.name: Tim Hardly's pole sign, Grafton Street
monuments._comment: From Joe's photo from the Riverside Drive lights looking down Grafton Street (2026-11-24): the coffee shop's tall pole sign at the edge of its lot by the westbound lanes, the red board over a black 'Drive Thru'. Drawn by tools/make_entrance_signs.py.

monuments.name: Windy's pole sign, Grafton Street
monuments._comment: From Joe's photo from the Riverside Drive lights looking down Grafton Street (2026-11-24): next to Tim Hardly's, further down Grafton, the white board over a reader board. Drawn by tools/make_entrance_signs.py.

monuments.name: Tim Hardly's pole sign, University Avenue
monuments._comment: From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue from the Superstore at Belvedere to Kirkwood Mews (2026-11-24): the coffee shop's red pole sign just past the Nassau Street lights, as on Grafton Street

monuments.name: Canadian flag at MacDougall's, University Avenue
monuments._comment: From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue from the Superstore at Belvedere to Kirkwood Mews (2026-11-24): two flags on tall poles by MacDougall's driveway

monuments.name: Island flag at MacDougall's, University Avenue
monuments._comment: From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue from the Superstore at Belvedere to Kirkwood Mews (2026-11-24): the Island's flag beside the Canadian one

monuments.name: Old Protestant Burying Ground fence, University Avenue
monuments._comment: From Joe's photos driving on south down University Avenue to Euston Street (2026-11-24): the black iron fence along the old burying ground on the left, at the back of the sidewalk.

_heritage_comment: heritage_district_m: buildings and streets within this many metres of the origin get the downtown look (Victorian brick blocks and shopfronts, black cast-iron lamp posts). Elsewhere: houses, plain modern boxes for big buildings, and street lights on wooden poles.

brands._comment: World brands: made-up businesses that stand in for real chains, the way the cars do (Hanaka, Toyola, Fjord). Each lists the real chains it replaces, matched by the OSM brand or name of a building, so every location changes at once. Colours echo the real chain's (sign_colour is the board, sign_text the letters) so players know what it is; the names and logos are our own and new ones follow as OSM maps them. 'kind' picks the usual look from brand_kinds; anything set here wins. To rename a brand, change its key (the name on the sign and in notes). Height and roof still come from the lidar. 'posters' lists artwork (textures/ads/, drawn by tools/make_ads.py) put up in the shop's front windows.

Tim Hardly's._comment: Never quite what you ordered. Window posters from tools/make_ads.py (textures/ads/).

MacDougall's._comment: Open all night for everyone too far gone for the Canton or China Garden; breakfast until 11, not 11:01.

Windy's._comment: Split from Tim Hardly's and now sells breakfast too, badly; no burgers before 11.

Hanaka._comment: Our Honda: the Civique, the Interlude (a Prelude) and the CR-Eh (a CR-V). Honda's red on a white board, so it doesn't read as Toyola's red board.

Toyola._comment: Our Toyota (Toyota crossed with Corolla): the Corollary, the Pious (a Prius) and the Haulux (an 80s Hilux). Toyota red.

Dodgy._comment: Our Dodge and Chrysler: the Jaunt, the Rammer 1500, the Caravel (a Grand Caravan) and the Charlatan SRT (a Charger). Dodge red.

Nissun._comment: Our Nissan: the Rouge (a Rogue) and the Sylph 240 (a 240SX).

Hyunsung._comment: Our Hyundai: the Ironiq 5 (an Ioniq 5) and the Filly (an 80s Pony).

Kayo._comment: Our Kia: say it fast and it's Kia-o; a kayo is a knockout, which suits the make of the Gadfly GT (a Stinger). Also the Sole (a Soul, a shoebox on wheels).

Suburoo._comment: Our Subaru: suburb plus kangaroo, the Outback make in every suburban driveway. The Hinterland (an Outback) and the Imprezzo WRZ (a WRX STI).

General Motives._comment: Our GMC and Buick (General Motors, with motives): the Yukoner (a Yukon) and the Roadmeister Estate (a Roadmaster wagon). The only GM lot in town is Hillside, built as Chevalet (see landmark 605896236), which sells these too.

Fjord._comment: Our Ford: the Halfton 150 (the game's pickup), the Pony GT, the Crown Vista (a Crown Victoria) and the Bucko (a Bronco). Ford blue, and a lot of trucks.

Chevalet._comment: Our Chevrolet: the gold of the bowtie on a dark board. The Cavalcade (a Cavalier) and the Camarillo IROQ (an 80s Camaro), plus General Motives' Yukoner and Roadmeister, since the real dealer sells GMC and Buick under the same roof.

Countess Auto._comment: Tools, tarps, a 40-piece socket set missing the one you need, and a surplus aisle nobody can explain.

brand_kinds._comment: The usual look for each kind of world brand; a brand's own settings win. Keys are the same as a landmark's (style, colour, roof_colour, trim, shop, awning, sign_colour, sign_text, sign_height, cornice) plus front: parking puts the sign on the side facing the car park, otherwise the street.

gas._comment: pylon: the price sign out by the road beside the canopy (a station's own landmark entry can set its own).

car dealer._comment: showroom: a tall glass showroom out front with a portal in the make's colour, service doors and a pylon by the road ; the lot gets about 18 cars for sale from 'stock' (model ids in scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd, repeat one to stock more of it).

fences._comment: Chain-link fences round mapped areas, by the area's OSM name: height (m), barbed (three strands of barbed wire on top), inset_m (how far inside the mapped edge it runs). Gaps are left where streets and driveways cross. riprap: a bank of armour stone outside the fence where it runs within within_m of the street (height, width).

Irving Oil Charlottetown Marine Terminal._comment: From Joe's photo from the Grafton Street Tim Hortons: a tall chain-link fence round the tank yard along Riverside Drive.

riprap._comment: The yard is banked up on armour stone along Riverside Drive, with the fence along the top. From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive.

Charlottetown Pollution Control Plant._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. Chain-link along Riverside Drive.

median_lights._comment: Divided roads that get a row of tall twin-arm street lights down the median, spacing in metres. From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant.

area_styles._comment: Looks for everything inside a named mapped area: buildings (landmark settings given to every building in it that has no entry of its own) and basins (every pond in it becomes a treatment tank with a concrete wall and railing; basin_height, basin_colour).

Charlottetown Pollution Control Plant._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. Low brown-brick buildings behind a chain-link fence, open tanks.

sign_gantries._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. The green signs over the northbound lanes before the Exhibition Drive roundabout, and the yellow roundabout sign.
sign_gantries.heading: north

highway_power_lines._comment: Highways (which otherwise get no power poles) that have a line of wooden poles and wires along one side: on the outer side of the carriageway heading the given way, offset_m out past its shoulder. From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive.

street_power_lines._comment: Town streets with more than the usual single line of poles: both_sides puts a line of wooden poles and wires down each side (the far side's poles carry the street lights there), heavy strings the main road's bundle (three on the crossarm, a neutral, and telephone and cable lines low on the road side), downtown keeps them inside heritage_district_m, where other streets' wires are buried. From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue from the Superstore all the way to Euston Street (2026-11-24): a heavy line along the west side, right at the back of the sidewalk, and another down the east side, the whole way.

curb_parking._comment: Main roads (which otherwise get no parked cars) with a few cars along both curbs, about odds of the spaces taken, on their two-way stretches of at most max_lanes lanes. From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue (2026-11-24): cars parked along the curb here and there from Allen Street down to Euston Street, where it narrows to a lane each way and a turn lane; none on the four-lane stretch to the north.

busy_lots._comment: Parking lots that are never empty: stalls within reach_m of the named street get a parked car in about odds of them, and lots there too small or unmapped for stall rows (store land drawn as asphalt, a drive-through's strip of parking) get rows laid out (seeded by the stall, so the same cars are there every time; cars on a dealer's lot are its stock instead). From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue (2026-11-24): the plaza, the drive-throughs, the muffler and tire shops and the grocery lots along it are all busy at lunchtime.
